clue.text: See 13
Object in cooker: this might be hidden!

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word's letters are placed inside the second's

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Something is lurking in the oven, and it might be hidden there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the phrase 'hidden agenda', a concealed plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a familiar idiom for a secret motive, so the answer is the thing that might be hidden.

clue.text: Fiona maybe to advance, renouncing PR

indicators.note: to renounce something is to give it up, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: to progress is to move forward
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone called Fiona is urged to get on in her career while giving up public relations.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiona is the princess in the Shrek films who turns out to be an ogre; 'maybe' marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Fiona in Shrek is a female ogre, so she is one example of the answer.

clue.text: Blade made with three metals

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium, the first metal
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel, the second metal
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, the third metal

explanation.surface: A blade forged from an alloy of three metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a cutting tool consisting essentially of a blade with a handle.

clue.text: You must meet Hindu god in Jewish school

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
Shiva is the Hindu god of destruction

explanation.surface: A visitor is told to meet a Hindu deity inside a Jewish school, an unlikely encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeshiva is an Orthodox Jewish college for the study of the Talmud and other religious texts.

clue.text: Leading club optimistic

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead or leading
to club is to beat with a stick

explanation.surface: The football club at the top of the table is feeling positive.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat is an informal synonym for cheerful and hopeful about the future.

clue.text: Excitedly at it during play? It affects growth

indicators.note: doing something excitedly means in an agitated, jumbled way, so the following letters are thrown about

parts.note: every letter of these four words is the raw material

explanation.surface: Children going at it hard while playing, which is how they grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'at it during play' is the fodder, not just 'at it'; the question mark covers the playful surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This small gland at the base of the brain secretes growth hormone, so it controls how the body grows.

clue.text: Yours truly picked up good girl — reader's assistant?

indicators.note: picking something up can mean catching it with the ear, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, I, which sounds the same as the organ of sight
G is the standard abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A man fetches a nice young woman to help someone who is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle or single lens worn to help eyesight, so it assists someone reading.

clue.text: Go without an item of underwear in burlesque

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try
the indefinite article
in Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt

explanation.surface: A burlesque dancer is told to perform minus one piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it means outside: TR(A VEST)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a mocking imitation, and a travesty is likewise a grotesque or absurd parody of something.

clue.text: Most ancient ateliers renovated

indicators.note: renovated things are rebuilt and rearranged, so the word's letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written; an atelier is an artist's workshop

explanation.surface: The oldest artists' studios have been done up.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest is the superlative of early, meaning first in time and so the oldest.

clue.text: Teetotallers outside followed by goddess

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so these letters go round the next part

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members do not drink
then means next in order, as when one thing is followed by another

explanation.surface: A group of non-drinkers is shadowed by a divine female figure.
explanation.walkthrough: AA stands for Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members are teetotallers, and the pair of letters split to go round the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Several coming before spirit, grotesque demon in film

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted and misshapen, so the word that follows is twisted out of shape

parts.note: a few means a small number, several
go means vigour or spirit, as in 'full of go'
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A horror-film review: several characters precede a ghost and a hideous monster.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1992 courtroom drama starring Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson is a well-known Hollywood movie.

clue.text: Feel bird, not rook, is flapping in amazement

indicators.note: flapping wings move wildly, so the remaining letters are tossed into a new order
'not' tells us to leave out the chess piece, which crossword setters abbreviate to a single letter

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for a rook
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone touches a bird other than a rook and it flaps about, to their astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from FEEL BIRD, add IS, then rearrange all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in disbelief is to be unable to credit what you see, much as being in amazement.

clue.text: Should my sibling adopt that mischievous child …

definitions.text: Should my sibling adopt that mischievous child

parts.words: Should my sibling adopt that mischievous child
parts.note: surface reading: musing on a brother or sister taking in a naughty youngster
setter's reading: a mischievous child is called a little monkey

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what would follow if their brother or sister adopted a naughty little kid.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis invites the speaker's conclusion, which is also a stock exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic cry of surprise, and literally describes the relation to a sibling's adopted little monkey.

clue.text: Atahualpa say almost eaten by lion?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: something eaten by an animal ends up in it
a lion is a big cat, and the word cat loses its last letter

explanation.surface: The Inca emperor Atahualpa nearly devoured by a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eaten by lion' is read as 'in cat', with the question mark flagging lion as an example of a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Atahualpa was the last emperor of the Inca Empire before the Spanish conquest, so he is an example.

clue.text: Last-but-one batter in Starmer's residence?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket eleven players bat in order, so the tenth is the second-to-last
second meaning: 10 Downing Street, home of the British prime minister Keir Starmer

explanation.surface: A cricketer near the bottom of the order is staying at the Prime Minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team has eleven batters; Number Ten is also the everyday name for 10 Downing Street, the UK prime minister's official home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a batting position in cricket and the Downing Street address of the prime minister.

clue.text: Something unknown in humour about bowlers?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: wit is clever humour
bowlers are hard round felt hats

explanation.surface: A puzzling joke about cricket bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers suggests cricket, but here they are hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit is a colloquial placeholder for a thing whose name you can't recall.

clue.text: Prayer somehow anguished, hard to be ignored

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of arranging things, so the letters are reordered
the abbreviation for hard is to be ignored, meaning left out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An anguished prayer, said with difficulty, that can't be ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Latin for 'Lamb of God', is a prayer said or sung in the Christian Mass.

clue.text: See 25
See 11
Nearby sound made by horse expending energy

indicators.note: expending means using up, so the letter for energy is spent and removed

parts.note: the cry a horse makes
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired horse panting near by.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old or literary word meaning near or close at hand.

clue.text: Indian state welcoming Yankee painter

indicators.note: a place welcoming a guest takes them in, so the state's letters enclose the next one

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian state hosts an American painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: Covered in dirt a Conservative gives scowl

indicators.note: to be covered in something is to be enclosed by it, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: grime is ingrained dirt
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, smeared with muck, frowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain, much like a scowl.

clue.text: Corrupt oil bid: one's appetite for it?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are distorted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dodgy oil tender: what drives someone to want it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a coy word for sex, and the question mark flags that saucy reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, and 'it' is a familiar euphemism for sex.

clue.text: Be annoyed and stop when you do this?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: drivers halt on noticing a traffic light at its danger colour

explanation.surface: Advice to someone getting cross: halt when it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as a literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become angry, and literally a motorist must halt on spotting a red light.

clue.text: See 13
Nanook at last hooks gigantic eel, possibly in great demand!

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, while the answer is a verb phrase meaning selling quickly

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters
at last points to the final letter of the name it follows

parts.note: the final letter of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Inuit fisherman finally lands a monster eel, and everyone wants a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanook evokes Nanook of the North, the Inuit hunter of the 1922 documentary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going like hot cakes sells fast because everybody wants it, which is the idiom for high demand.

clue.text: See 6
Sioux sent back satisfactory inside information

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: data are facts or information

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: OK means acceptable or satisfactory

explanation.surface: A Sioux warrior returns with a decent piece of intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dakota are one of the main divisions of the Sioux peoples of the North American plains.

clue.text: Incautious taking wine and pork pie before run

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
in Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie, or porky, is a lie
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A reckless eater helping himself to wine and a pork pie before going for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang: 'pork pie' rhymes with 'lie', so a porky is a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and careless, showing a lack of proper concern or caution.

clue.text: Silly to eat son's bananas

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the first word swallows the next letter

parts.note: inane means silly or senseless
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: It's daft to scoff your boy's fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being eaten, but it is the slang definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is informal slang for mad or crazy, the same as being out of one's mind.

clue.text: Useless personnel for city in South 27

definitions.meaning: first meaning: staff who contribute nothing
second meaning: a historic gold-rush town in South Dakota, reading 27 as its answer

explanation.surface: A company's dead-weight staff are being sent off to a city out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27-across, so the place is in South Dakota, the Wild West town of Wild Bill Hickok's death.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadwood is idiom for unproductive members of an organisation and the name of a famous South Dakota town.
